notice: Candidate mapping from Grundschutz++ requirement IDs to Azure controls. No information-security expert has reviewed it. It is not a compliance statement. It holds requirement IDs, modal verbs, security levels and our own mapping only; read the requirement text in your local catalogue extract.

policy_source.note: Built-in policy definition IDs, display names, versions and allowed effects were read from this commit (28 Oct 2026). Check them again before you deploy: built-in definitions change.

themes.title: Data location and jurisdiction
themes.summary: Where data is stored, and which jurisdiction governs the provider.

themes.title: Provider assurance
themes.summary: Third-party evidence that the provider's own controls work, such as a C5 or ISO/IEC 27001 attestation. Provider scope only.

themes.title: Encryption in transit
themes.summary: Network traffic to and between services is encrypted, and weak protocols are switched off.

themes.title: Encryption at rest
themes.summary: Stored data is encrypted, optionally with keys the customer controls.

themes.title: Security logging
themes.summary: Security-relevant events reach a log store the organisation controls.

themes.title: Privileged access
themes.summary: Powerful accounts and external access use strong, multi-factor sign-in.

themes.title: Network exposure
themes.summary: Workloads are not directly reachable from, or directly connected to, public networks unless their archetype allows it.

themes.title: Backup and restore
themes.summary: Data is backed up, stored redundantly and restorable.

themes.title: Vulnerabilities and patches
themes.summary: Vulnerabilities are found and handled, and patch status is monitored.

themes.title: Data inventory and classification
themes.summary: Data is inventoried and assigned a protection-need class by its owner.

themes.title: Exception handling
themes.summary: Every exception is authorised by a named person and documented with its reason.

controls.name: Allowed locations
Allowed locations for resource groups
controls.note: Evaluates the resource groups that hold the application.

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state of the location assignments, and the allowed-locations parameter of the archetype.
requirements.gap: Azure Policy enforces the deployment region of regional resources. Resources with location 'global' and the provider's jurisdiction need a written record.

controls.name: Contractual data-location and jurisdiction commitments of the provider, referenced in the repository

requirements.evidence: Reference to the signed contract terms and the provider's data-residency commitments, with review date.
requirements.gap: A contract is not resource configuration; no policy can check it.

controls.name: Provider's third-party attestation (for example a C5 type 2 report) obtained from the provider's trust portal and referenced in the repository

requirements.evidence: Attestation reference, scope, period covered and expiry date.
requirements.gap: Covers the provider's scope only. The customer's controls are covered by the other themes.

controls.name: Recurring review of the provider's attestation and its bridge letters, recorded in the repository

requirements.evidence: Review record with reviewer role, date and result.
requirements.gap: The review is a human activity; Azure exposes no control for it.

controls.name: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
App Service apps should only be accessible over HTTPS
Azure SQL Database should be running TLS version 1.2 or newer

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state per resource.
requirements.gap: Services that the application runs inside virtual machines are not evaluated.

controls.name: Storage accounts should have the specified minimum TLS version
App Service apps should use the latest TLS version
Azure SQL Database should be running TLS version 1.2 or newer

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state per resource.
requirements.gap: The App Service TLS definition can only audit, not deny.

applies_when.otherwise: The application keeps no data of its own.

controls.name: Service-side encryption at rest with platform-managed keys, on by default for Azure Storage and Azure SQL
Storage accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption
SQL servers should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state of the customer-managed-key definitions; platform encryption needs no evidence beyond the service documentation.
requirements.gap: Platform encryption is always on and cannot be audited per resource. The policies check customer-managed keys, which is stronger than the requirement asks; the storage definition can only audit.

controls.name: Audit diagnostic setting for selected resource types
Enable logging by category group for App Service (microsoft.web/sites) to Log Analytics
Enable logging by category group for Key vaults (microsoft.keyvault/vaults) to Log Analytics
Enable logging by category group for SQL databases (microsoft.sql/servers/databases) to Log Analytics
Configure diagnostic settings for Storage Accounts to Log Analytics workspace

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state of the diagnostic-setting assignments, and the Log Analytics workspace that receives the logs.
requirements.gap: Policy routes platform resource logs. Which events the application itself writes, and guest operating-system events on virtual machines, stay with the application owner.

controls.name: Configure Azure Activity logs to stream to specified Log Analytics workspace
Microsoft Entra audit logs exported to the same workspace by a diagnostic setting

requirements.evidence: Activity log and Entra audit log entries for role assignments and privileged changes in the workspace.
requirements.gap: Privileged actions inside the application are logged only if the application writes them.

controls.name: Configure Azure Activity logs to stream to specified Log Analytics workspace

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state and the diagnostic setting on the subscription.

controls.name: Conditional Access policy that requires phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for privileged directory and Azure roles
Privileged Identity Management: just-in-time activation of privileged roles with multi-factor authentication
Users must authenticate with multi-factor authentication to create or update resources

requirements.evidence: Exported Conditional Access and role settings; Entra sign-in logs; policy compliance state of the resource-write definition.
requirements.gap: Azure Policy sees only resource writes by users; it cannot see sign-ins, service principals or directory roles. Enforcement sits in Microsoft Entra.

applies_when.otherwise: The application is not reachable from external networks.

controls.name: Conditional Access policy with a phishing-resistant authentication strength for the application's sign-ins from external networks

requirements.evidence: Exported Conditional Access policy and Entra sign-in logs.
requirements.gap: Sign-in requirements are not resource configuration; Azure Policy cannot check them.

controls.name: Network interfaces should not have public IPs
Storage accounts should disable public network access
Public network access on Azure SQL Database should be disabled
Azure Key Vault should disable public network access

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state per resource.
requirements.gap: The requirement concerns direct connections to public networks. The policies remove public endpoints; outbound traffic control is a firewall and routing concern of the platform hub and is not evaluated.

applies_when.otherwise: The application has no virtual network of its own.

controls.name: Subnets should be associated with a Network Security Group
controls.note: Evaluates a Microsoft Defender for Cloud assessment; check that your tenant produces it without a paid plan (unverified).

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state per subnet.
requirements.gap: The policy checks that a network security group exists, not that its rules restrict connections.

applies_when.otherwise: The application keeps no data of its own.

controls.name: Azure Backup should be enabled for Virtual Machines
Automated backups of Azure SQL Database, on by default

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state for virtual machines; backup configuration of databases and storage from the backup vault.
requirements.gap: No built-in definition in this slice audits backup of storage accounts or App Service content.

applies_when.otherwise: The application keeps no data of its own.

controls.name: Geo-redundant storage should be enabled for Storage Accounts
Long-term geo-redundant backup should be enabled for Azure SQL Databases

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state per resource.
requirements.gap: Geo-redundancy must stay inside the allowed locations; check the paired region against the data-location parameter.

applies_when.otherwise: The application keeps no data of its own.

controls.name: Restore test on a representative sample, recorded in the repository by the application owner

requirements.evidence: Restore-test record with date, sample, result and tester role.
requirements.gap: A restore test is an activity, not a configuration.

applies_when.otherwise: No virtual machines: the provider patches the platform of the PaaS services.

controls.name: Machines should be configured to periodically check for missing system updates

requirements.evidence: Policy compliance state per machine, and the update assessment results.

controls.name: Documented vulnerability-scan procedure with evaluation and handling, recorded in the repository
A vulnerability assessment solution should be enabled on your virtual machines
controls.note: Passes only with a vulnerability assessment solution, such as a paid Microsoft Defender for Servers plan. Optional in this lab.

controls.name: Microsoft Defender for Cloud vulnerability findings

requirements.evidence: The procedure document and, where a scanner runs, its findings export.
requirements.gap: Defender for Cloud gives posture signals, not enforcement, and its scanners need a paid plan. Without one, the procedure is evidenced by attestation only.

applies_when.otherwise: The application keeps no data of its own.

controls.name: Protection-need class assigned by the data owner and recorded in the application profile
Require a tag on resources
controls.note: Use the tag name data-classification. A tag shows that a class was recorded, not that it is right.

controls.name: Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and data map classification

requirements.evidence: Owner's classification in the application profile; tag compliance state; label reports where Purview is licensed.
requirements.gap: Classifying data is an owner's judgement. Policy checks only that a tag exists; Purview needs a licence and is optional in this lab.

applies_when.otherwise: The application keeps no data of its own.

controls.name: Information inventory kept with the application profile and reviewed by the data owner
Azure Resource Graph inventory of the resources that hold the data
Microsoft Purview data map

requirements.evidence: Inventory record with review date; Resource Graph export of the data stores.
requirements.gap: Resource Graph lists data stores, not the information inside them.

controls.name: Every exception is a pull request approved by a named person in the authorising role, enforced by branch protection and code owners

requirements.evidence: Pull-request approval history.
requirements.gap: Branch protection proves who approved, not that the approver had the authority; the authorising role is a governance decision.

controls.name: Exception record in the repository with justification, risk owner and expiry date, checked by a pull-request workflow
Azure Policy exemption with description, category and expiry, created only from the approved record

requirements.evidence: Exception records and the matching Azure Policy exemptions.
requirements.gap: Azure Policy exemptions make the expiry date optional; only exemptions raised through the pull-request check are guaranteed to have one.
